text: -1-y PFS is 66.7% with FMT and 35.0% without-mOS was not reached vs. 25.3 (95% CI, 17.1–33.6) months with FMT and placebo, respectively-Only 1 placebo group discontinued with grade 3 AE There are several ongoing trials investigating the role of FMT in combination with ICI for cancer therapy. In the genitourinary space, the MITRIC (NCT05286294) and TACITO (NCT04758507) trials are investigating FMT in combination with ICI for patients with advanced cancer. The MIRTIC (NCT05286294) trial plans to enroll 20 patients with progressive solid tumor malignancy on ICI therapy who will receive FMT from ICI-responders with a greater than 12-month response.^{48} Patients will receive up to 5 cycles of FMT and continue ICI treatment, subsequently analyzing safety, objective tumor response, and other outcomes. While this trial is ongoing, preliminary results have been reported for 9 patients: 6 with melanoma, 1 with RCC, 1 with pancreatic cancer, and 1 with head and neck cutaneous cancer.^{48} All the patients have received at least one FMT, with 8 of 9 receiving 2, and 5 patients currently have recorded stable disease as the best response. The FMT-related adverse events were all grade 1. Although these results are preliminary and the study is ongoing, current results show that FMT combined with continued ICI therapy can be feasible and safe.^{48} The TACITO (NCT04758507) trial is investigating FMT for patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) receiving immunotherapy.^{49} Patients with mRCC are randomized to axitinib plus pembrolizumab with FMT from a patient with complete and lasting response to immunotherapy or placebo.^{49} Patients received FMT administered via colonoscopy and subsequently FMT via oral capsules at days 90 and 180. The endpoints included PFS, overall survival (OS), and the objective response rate (ORR). Preliminary results presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology Congress 2024 demonstrated that patients treated with FMT had a 1-y PFS rate of 66.7% compared to 35.0% in the control group (n = 50 total patients).^{49} The study also noted an ORR of 54% in the FMT group compared to 28% in the placebo group. These preliminary results also highlighted the role of FMT increasing the activity and therapeutic response of immunotherapy in mRCC patients.^{49} Similar studies evaluating the combination of FMT and immunotherapy are being conducted for prostate cancer (NCT04116775, an ongoing phase II trial) and lung cancer (NCT04924374, NCT04951583, and NCT05502913).^{50–53} Interestingly, NCT04924374 has no bowel preparation involved, whereas NCT04951583 employs bowel preparation via polyethylene glycol administration, and NCT05502913 is exploring administration of FMT via colonoscopy and oral capsules. Additionally, multiple trials are ongoing in the GI cancer space exploring FMT and immunotherapy including NCT04130763, NCT04729322, and NCT04975217.^{54–56} NCT04729322 is investigating the efficacy of FMT for patients with colorectal cancer receiving anti-PD-1, using an antibiotic based bowel preparation with metronidazole, vancomycin, and neomycin.^{55} NCT04975217 is investigating FMT administered via oral capsules during colonoscopy to assess incidence of immune-related adverse events in patients with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.^{56} There are several other trials in the early stages investigating the role of FMT in immuno-oncology, and several more that are in the planning stages. The PERFORM (NCT04163289) trial is assessing if FMT from healthy donors can impact and/or prevent immune related adverse effects.^{57} Preliminary results have been reported in a group of 10 patients with mRCC who received FMT from healthy donors, showing an associated safety profile and promising clinical efficacy data.^{57} Multiple studies (Table 2) are ongoing that are exploring various microbiome interventions for patients with UC undergoing ICI as well as exploring microbiome signatures as possible predictive tools for ICI responders that will be fruitful and informative for UC patients.
